summary: Two flagged events show malformed requests sent from ip-01 to host-01, consistent with a fuzzing activity.

sequence.description: Malformed requests were sent from ip-01 to host-01.
Additional malformed requests were sent from ip-01 to host-01.

findings.statement: Fuzzing activity was detected on host-01 from source IP ip-01.

recommendations: Investigate the source IP ip-01 to determine if it is a known internal fuzzer or an external threat. Why: The events show malformed requests from ip-01 to host-01 (fx-021, fx-022). Determining the origin helps assess if this is authorized testing or malicious activity.

Review the logs on host-01 for any signs of successful exploitation or system instability following the malformed requests. Why: Fuzzing aims to find vulnerabilities. Checking for crashes or unexpected behavior on host-01 (fx-021, fx-022) helps determine if the fuzzing was effective.
risk_justification: The risk score is low (24) because the events show only the initiation of fuzzing (malformed requests) without evidence of successful exploitation, data exfiltration, or system compromise.
uncertainty: It is not known if the fuzzing resulted in any successful exploitation or system compromise on host-01. (would be settled by: System logs from host-01 showing crashes, errors, or unauthorized access attempts following the timestamps of fx-021 and fx-022.) It is not known if ip-01 is an authorized internal fuzzer or an external attacker. (would be settled by: Network access control lists, internal asset inventory, or fuzzer registration records.) Limitations: The analysis is based solely on the provided evidence package and does not include real-time system state or historical context beyond the listed events. The context event fx-023 (remote login by user-01) is not linked to the fuzzing events in the data and is not considered part of the attack sequence.
